scope: Independent live issue reads only; no issue mutation. Source issues 197-199 are intentionally open; operational issue 200 correction and closure are assessed separately.

issues.body:
The round 62 carrollite source dossier identified DOI [10.1016/j.hydromet.2021.105592](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.hydromet.2021.105592), Cameron et al., *Stirred-tank bioleaching of nickel and cobalt from pyrrhotite-rich tailings from Sudbury, Ontario*. Round 63 verified its metadata and obtained related public material, but did not obtain the complete original article or its inherited experimental protocol.

The publisher's available text delegates key methods to the COM 2017 contribution **Stirred-Tank Bioleaching of a Pyrrhotite-Rich Tailings Sample**, paper 9704. The openly acquired COM 2017 file is only a table of contents. Elsevier's public API returned metadata, not full text. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar did not supply an accessible original. Later mine-backfill proceedings concern other tests and do not replace these methods. The similarly titled 2018 chapter DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-95022-8_225 is a related lead, not proof of the 2017 protocol.

Follow-up work:

- Obtain legitimate complete copies of the 2021 paper, COM 2017 paper 9704 and any linked supplements; preserve acquisition dates and hashes.
- Resolve tailings process origin, feed preparation and magnetic upgrading before mapping to the existing nickel-flotation-tailings owner. Do not create a locality-only owner or assign mixed-feed yields to pyrrhotite or pentlandite mineral records.
- Verify inoculum membership/strain evidence, medium and operating conditions, controls, denominator and mass-balance accounting, original tables/figures and any correction notices.
- Distinguish dissolved-metal extraction from physically isolated recovery; later pilot statements are not industrial deployment evidence.
- Add a reviewed extension only if complete primary evidence supports it. The accepted round 63 thesis assays are a different experiment and do not close this gap.

Deduplication: searched all 122 saved GitHub issue entries, including bodies and closed issues, for the exact DOI, Cameron, pyrrhotite-rich, nickel tailings/slag/smelter and related thesis identifiers; no matching issue was found. The source dossier will be linked in the publication handoff. This is a bounded source-acquisition gap, not a claim that no other useful nickel evidence exists.
issues.title: Acquire complete Cameron 2021 and COM 2017 methods before extending nickel-flotation-tailings

issues.body:
Obtain and inspect a legitimate complete original of Mavromatis et al. (2012), **Magnesium isotope fractionation during hydrous magnesium carbonate precipitation with and without cyanobacteria**, DOI [10.1016/j.gca.2011.10.019](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gca.2011.10.019), before adding a nesquehonite microbial mechanism or extending dypingite beyond its Atlin evidence.

Round 63 resolved the bibliographic identity and indexed abstract. The abstract reports no detectable microbial effect on bulk precipitation rate or Mg isotope fractionation under the tested Gloeocapsa conditions. The complete Open University PDF returned 403; CiteSeer redirected to an unavailable archived resource, UCL returned 404 and Southampton was inaccessible. A search-indexed PDF is not original-figure inspection. Do not infer the phase/time/biotic-control assignments from the abstract.

Acceptance checks:

- Preserve actual access route, UTC, version, rights and checksum; inspect complete methods, phase tables, XRD/other original figures and relevant supplements.
- Resolve nesquehonite versus dypingite assignments by time and treatment, abiotic controls, organism resolution, conditions and null outcomes.
- Deduplicate against existing material owners and the Atlin study; do not count shared phase arms as independent experiments or inherit magnesium criticality.
- Curate only supported claims, add actual history and independent saved scientific review, and run the required validation gates. An unchanged or deferred outcome is valid if evidence remains insufficient.

Handoff: `research/sources/round63-magnesium-carbonates/20261014T053338Z-source-investigation.{md,json}`. All 122 open/closed issues in the coordinator's round63 inventory were checked by exact DOI, names and target phases; no matching issue was found in that bounded snapshot.
issues.title: Acquire Mavromatis 2012 original for nesquehonite phase and null-effect assessment

issues.body:
Acquire and inspect complete primary culture evidence before creating a hydromagnesite microbial mechanism. Prioritize Sánchez-Román et al. (2011), **Aerobic biomineralization of Mg-rich carbonates: Implications for natural environments**, DOI [10.1016/j.chemgeo.2010.11.020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemgeo.2010.11.020). A second lead is Balci et al. (2016), **Reproducing Authigenic Carbonate Precipitation in the Hypersaline Lake Acıgöl (Turkey) with Microbial Cultures**, DOI [10.1080/01490451.2015.1099763](https://doi.org/10.1080/01490451.2015.1099763).

Round 63 verified hydromagnesite's September 2026 IMA row (grandfathered; 1828 is a description year, not an approval ID), but the Granada 2011 PDF returned 504 twice and the CSIC landing links a restricted-access notice. The 2016 source was metadata/abstract-only. Power 2009 DOI 10.1016/j.chemgeo.2009.01.012 was acquired as a complete author-hosted PDF but only bibliographic/abstract-screened this round; a full assessment may supply qualified field context, not automatically culture-level causality.

Acceptance checks:

- Retain legitimate original/supplement provenance, version, access time, rights and checksums; inspect methods, phase assignments, tables and original figures.
- Distinguish hydromagnesite from dypingite, nesquehonite and mixed carbonate products; preserve abiotic controls, assay conditions, strain/community resolution and null results.
- Do not infer an experimental product from a thermodynamic hydromagnesite proxy or inherit constituent-magnesium criticality.
- Deduplicate material identity and shared experiments, then add only supported claims with actual history, independent scientific review and validation. Keep an evidence-gap outcome if the primary does not support curation.

Handoff: `research/sources/round63-magnesium-carbonates/20261014T053338Z-source-investigation.{md,json}`. All 122 open/closed issues in the coordinator's round63 inventory were checked by exact DOIs, names and target phase; no matching issue was found in that bounded snapshot.
issues.title: Acquire hydromagnesite culture originals and verify phase-specific controls

issues.body:
Independent publication review found that the round 63 queue-admission helper binds the topic head but does not recheck live `main` against the reviewed base immediately before admission or validate the full stored preflight identity. A main advance can therefore be admitted, with the exact parent/tree mismatch detected only after merge. Severity: major / P2.

Evidence: `reviews/publication/20261014-round63/20261014T054836Z-publication-queue-finding.{md,json}` preserves the original helper hash and independent assessment. This is an operational publication finding, not a scientific record defect.

Acceptance criteria:

- Require a successful preflight of mode `preflight`, with the same trusted base, topic head and tree as the reviewed commit receipt; verify its command outcomes and retained log hash.
- Read live remote main immediately before queue admission and require equality with the reviewed base; retain the observation in the queue receipt.
- Exercise isolated regression cases for matching base, changed base, mismatched preflight identity and failed/tampered evidence without submitting a live queue request.
- Document the requirement in the maintained local publication profile so future session helpers inherit it.
- Preserve the original finding and save an independent successor disposition. Keep exact actual-merge tree/parent checks and fresh remote-main validation: a read-before-enqueue check is not atomic base locking.
issues.title: Recheck trusted main and full preflight identity before queue admission
